exclusions.A: Thirty years of Rusk's notes and my own, and it took your dates to show me the stove.
exclusions.D: He copied her list into the notebook under Rusk's last entry and wrote her name beside it.
exclusions.E: Thirty years of Rusk's notes and my own, and it took your dates to show me the stove.

WV10-P01.5.note: Abel credits Nell's dates with solving what thirty years of notes had not and writes her name in the notebook, which signals gratitude, not worry (it is ready), amusement, wistfulness, or indignation.

exclusions.A: One wet May morning, six men raised the canopy onto its centre pole.
exclusions.B: One wet May morning, six men raised the canopy onto its centre pole.
exclusions.D: One wet May morning, six men raised the canopy onto its centre pole.
exclusions.E: One wet May morning, six men raised the canopy onto its centre pole.

WV10-P02.4.note: Six men lifting a canopy onto a pole are hoisting it; 'reared' in its sense of erecting a structure is arguably defensible, while 'collected' and 'increased' borrow from the raffle sentence and do not fit a physical canopy.

exclusions.A: Hal took her out to the barn and stood a long while beside the grey, running his thumb along its chipped mane and telling her about the summers Edie had ridden it on the common, years before she died.
exclusions.C: Hal took her out to the barn and stood a long while beside the grey, running his thumb along its chipped mane and telling her about the summers Edie had ridden it on the common, years before she died.
exclusions.D: Then he went to fetch the trailer.
exclusions.E: Then he went to fetch the trailer.

WV10-P02.5.note: Hal lingers by the horse recalling his late sister's summers riding it before handing it over, which is nostalgia; fetching the trailer rules out indignation or worry, and nothing is playful or thankful.

exclusions.E: She looked at it a long time, then said she used to stand there in the dark just to hear them pass, and that the sound had been gone since the slats went up.

WV10-P03.5.note: Gazing at a photo from her first summer and recalling a sound now gone is wistful longing; her reply does not speak to the future, so it is not worry, and it shows no playfulness, irritation, or admiration of anyone.
